column1: # Target paradigms: what `inflect` should return for the cases where the
# printed tables pack two distinctions into one cell. Hand-checked, and the
# authority — where this file and the engine disagree, the engine is wrong.
# Columns: FORM, LEMMA, UPOS, XPOS, FEATS. Blocks are separated by a blank line
# and headed by the dictionary row they come from. FEATS is alphabetical, `_`
# Lines marked `# fix:` are where this file already differs from what the engine
# fix: four cells hold two forms, and they are not free variants: `telęte` is
# fix: the athematic declension the grammar keeps as an option, `telęta` the
# fix: ordinary neuter one, declined as if the nominative were `teleto`.
# fix: Same stem, different endings — so the feature goes on the ending's
# fix: origin, not on the stem.
# fix: same as `telę`: `matere` is the athematic genitive, `materi` the one
# fix: `mati` gets when it is declined like `kost`, which the grammar names as
# fix: fourteen cells, every one of them a pair — and it is the same pair as
# fix: `telę`, spread over the whole word instead of four oblique cells. The
# fix: grammar says it outright: `kamen` is the athematic masculine, and
# fix: `kamenj` is what you get by declining it like an ordinary one (gen.
# fix: `kamenja`, dat. `kamenju`). So the hard column carries Athematic and the
# fix: soft one carries nothing, citation form included.
# fix: The lemma stays `kamenj` for both. A second dictionary entry would not
# fix: help: the table builds both columns from either spelling, so `kamen` and
# fix: Variant=Long/Short kept for the contraction, which is real and runs
# fix: through four cells — 2sg, 3sg, 1pl, 2pl. The 3pl `dělajųt` has no
# fix: contracted counterpart and stays unmarked, which is the same rule as
# fix: everywhere else: mark a contrast, not its absence.
# fix: The first person singular is a different alternation and now says so.
# fix: `dělam` is not the short half of a pair with `dělajem` — that form does
# fix: not exist — it is the 3sg plus the `-m` of `jesm`, exactly like `barvim`
# fix: and `nesem`. One length test used to stand in for both distinctions;
# fix: contraction is 1550 verbs × 4 cells, the `-m` ending is every verb, 3847.
# fix: `barvęt` have no second form — so it is not a class dividing the
# fix: paradigm, it is one ending beside another in one cell. `-m` comes from
# fix: the athematic `jesm`, `dam`, `jem`, `věm`, so that is what it is called.
# fix: Measured across the whole list: the doublet exists in 3847 cells, and in
# fix: every one of them the second member is the 3sg plus `m` — no exceptions,
# fix: no verb with a third reading. Finding it is positional and total.
# fix: Variant=Long/Short dropped, the order swapped, Athematic added. Length
# fix: had picked the wrong winner here — `nesem` is longer than `nesų`, so it
# fix: came out as the long form of a contraction this verb does not have.
# fix: Same shape as `barvjų / barvim`, annotated the same way.
# fix: Animacy added. The masculine accusative right above splits animate from
# fix: inanimate; the neuter cell holds the same two forms and the same split
# fix: (neuter animates exist — `telę`, `ditę`), but the channel is only wired
# fix: for masculine, so the pair came out indistinguishable.
# fix: PrepCase replaces the Variant=Bound this file used to carry. `jego` and
# fix: `njego` are the same word in two environments and neither works in the
# fix: other's — you cannot say `do jego` and you cannot say `njego vidim` — so
# fix: both members get a value, which is what UD's PrepCase is for.
# fix: The clitic is a different axis and keeps Variant=Short: `go` is the
# fix: unstressable form, and it has no `n-` counterpart at all.
# fix: LEMMA and FORM answer different questions. Every third-person entry —
# fix: `jej`, `jų`, `jih`, `jim` — declines by its own column and is called
# fix: `on`, which is the lemma every Slavic treebank gives these forms. The
# fix: entry keeps its ten or twelve forms; it does not swell to the whole
# fix: paradigm just because the name is shared.
# fix: the locative has no bare form. The grammar says it outright: the locative
# fix: is always governed by a preposition, so `jem` never occurs and only
# fix: `njem` is a word. Same for `njej` and `njih`, and for `iže`.
# No Number, on purpose. Number here is agreement morphology — which number's
# endings a form carries — not the quantity a word names. `pęť` gets Number=Sing
# because it declines as a feminine singular, `četvero` Plur because its endings
# are plural ones; `dva` has gender columns and no number contrast at all, so
# there is nothing to record. Dual would be a claim that `dva` contrasts with a
# non-dual form of itself, which it does not: the two-ness is in the lemma.
# fix: NumType=Sets added on every row. `dva` above carries NumType=Card, the
# fix: collective numerals carry nothing at all, and a numeral with no NumType
# fix: is indistinguishable from a noun that happens to be tagged NUM.
# fix: Animacy added, same missed channel as `sam` — `četveryh` is the animate
# fix: accusative, `četvero` the inanimate one, and they came out identical.
